name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_RESPIRATIONINPLANTS_MATCH_Q01 - Enzymes and reactions in glycolysis and fermentation

questiontext.text:
Match the enzymes in List-I with the corresponding reactions they catalyse in List-II.

List-I (Enzyme)List-II (Reaction)
(A) Invertase(i) Reduction of pyruvic acid to lactic acid
(B) Hexokinase(ii) Conversion of sucrose into glucose and fructose
(C) Pyruvic acid decarboxylase(iii) Phosphorylation of glucose and fructose
(D) Lactate dehydrogenase(iv) Conversion of pyruvic acid to acetaldehyde and \(\text{CO}_2\) in yeast

Choose the correct match.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Each metabolic step in carbohydrate breakdown and fermentation is catalysed by a specific enzyme.

Step 2: Evaluation of Enzyme–Reaction Pairs
1. Invertase hydrolyses the disaccharide sucrose into glucose and fructose so that they can enter glycolysis.
2. Hexokinase phosphorylates glucose and fructose using ATP to form glucose-6-phosphate (and fructose-6-phosphate).
3. Pyruvic acid decarboxylase acts on pyruvic acid during alcoholic fermentation in yeast to release \(\text{CO}_2\) (leading to ethanol formation with alcohol dehydrogenase).
4. Lactate dehydrogenase reduces pyruvic acid to lactic acid in bacteria and in animal muscle cells during exercise under inadequate oxygen.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct pairings are: (A)–(ii), (B)–(iii), (C)–(iv), (D)–(i).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_RESPIRATIONINPLANTS_MATCH_Q02 - Sites of respiratory processes in plants

questiontext.text:
Match the respiratory processes or structures in List-I with their correct cellular or anatomical sites in List-II.

List-I (Process / Structure)List-II (Site)
(A) EMP pathway (Glycolysis)(i) Inner mitochondrial membrane
(B) Krebs' cycle(ii) Woody stems for gaseous exchange
(C) Electron Transport System(iii) Cytoplasm
(D) Lenticels(iv) Mitochondrial matrix

Choose the correct match.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Cellular respiration is compartmentalised across different regions of the eukaryotic cell, while gaseous exchange in plants occurs through surface openings.

Step 2: Evaluation of Process–Site Pairs
1. The EMP pathway (glycolysis) occurs in the cytoplasm of all living cells.
2. The Krebs' cycle (tricarboxylic acid cycle) takes place in the mitochondrial matrix.
3. The Electron Transport System (ETS) and oxidative phosphorylation are located on the inner mitochondrial membrane.
4. Lenticels are openings in the bark of thick, woody stems that permit gaseous exchange.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct pairings are: (A)–(iii), (B)–(iv), (C)–(i), (D)–(ii).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_RESPIRATIONINPLANTS_MATCH_Q03 - Energy and redox events in glycolysis

questiontext.text:
Match the glycolytic conversions in List-I with the corresponding events in List-II.

List-I (Conversion)List-II (Event)
(A) Glucose \(\rightarrow\) Glucose-6-phosphate(i) Direct synthesis of ATP
(B) PGAL \(\rightarrow\) BPGA(ii) Cleavage of 6C sugar into two 3C sugars
(C) BPGA \(\rightarrow\) 3-PGA(iii) Utilisation of ATP
(D) Fructose-1,6-bisphosphate \(\rightarrow\) PGAL + DHAP(iv) Formation of \(\text{NADH} + \text{H}^+\)

Choose the correct match.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Glycolysis consists of a preparatory phase where ATP is consumed and a payoff phase where \(\text{NADH} + \text{H}^+\) and ATP are generated.

Step 2: Evaluation of Glycolytic Events
1. Glucose is phosphorylated to glucose-6-phosphate with the utilisation of 1 ATP molecule.
2. Fructose-1,6-bisphosphate (6C) splits into two 3C triose phosphates: 3-phosphoglyceraldehyde (PGAL) and dihydroxyacetone phosphate (DHAP).
3. During the conversion of PGAL to 1,3-bisphosphoglycerate (BPGA), two redox equivalents are transferred to \(\text{NAD}^+\) to form \(\text{NADH} + \text{H}^+\).
4. The conversion of BPGA to 3-phosphoglyceric acid (3-PGA) is an energy-yielding step coupled to the direct synthesis of ATP.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct pairings are: (A)–(iii), (B)–(iv), (C)–(i), (D)–(ii).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_RESPIRATIONINPLANTS_MATCH_Q04 - Complexes of the mitochondrial electron transport system

questiontext.text:
Match the ETS complexes in List-I with their respective identities or prosthetic components in List-II.

List-I (Complex)List-II (Identity / Component)
(A) Complex I(i) Cytochrome \(bc_1\) complex
(B) Complex II(ii) Cytochrome \(c\) oxidase containing cytochromes \(a, a_3\) and two copper centres
(C) Complex III(iii) NADH dehydrogenase
(D) Complex IV(iv) Succinate dehydrogenase

Choose the correct match.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The mitochondrial electron transport system consists of four multi-protein redox complexes (Complexes I–IV) embedded in the inner mitochondrial membrane.

Step 2: Evaluation of Complex Identities
1. Complex I is NADH dehydrogenase, which oxidises NADH produced in the matrix and transfers electrons to ubiquinone.
2. Complex II is succinate dehydrogenase, which transfers reducing equivalents from \(\text{FADH}_2\) (generated during succinate oxidation) to ubiquinone.
3. Complex III is the cytochrome \(bc_1\) complex, which oxidises ubiquinol and passes electrons to cytochrome \(c\).
4. Complex IV is the cytochrome \(c\) oxidase complex containing cytochromes \(a\) and \(a_3\), along with two copper centres.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct pairings are: (A)–(iii), (B)–(iv), (C)–(i), (D)–(ii).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_RESPIRATIONINPLANTS_MATCH_Q05 - Respiratory substrates and respiratory quotient values

questiontext.text:
Match the respiratory substrates in List-I with their characteristic Respiratory Quotient (RQ) or metabolic feature in List-II.

List-I (Substrate)List-II (RQ / Feature)
(A) Carbohydrates (e.g., glucose)(i) \(\text{RQ} = 0.7\)
(B) Fats (e.g., tripalmitin)(ii) Enters glycolysis after conversion to PGAL
(C) Proteins(iii) \(\text{RQ} = 1.0\)
(D) Glycerol(iv) \(\text{RQ} \approx 0.9\)

Choose the correct match.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The respiratory quotient (\(\text{RQ} = \frac{\text{volume of } \text{CO}_2 \text{ evolved}}{\text{volume of } \text{O}_2 \text{ consumed}}\)) depends on the chemical composition of the respiratory substrate, while non-carbohydrate molecules enter the respiratory pathway at specific intermediates.

Step 2: Evaluation of Substrate Properties
1. When carbohydrates like glucose are completely oxidised, equal volumes of \(\text{CO}_2\) and \(\text{O}_2\) are evolved and consumed, giving \(\text{RQ} = 1.0\).
2. When fats like tripalmitin are used, \(\text{RQ} = \frac{102}{145} = 0.7\).
3. When proteins are used as respiratory substrates, the RQ is about \(0.9\).
4. Fats are broken down into fatty acids and glycerol; glycerol enters the respiratory pathway after being converted to PGAL.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct pairings are: (A)–(iii), (B)–(i), (C)–(iv), (D)–(ii).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_RESPIRATIONINPLANTS_MATCH_Q06 - Carbon skeletons of citric acid cycle intermediates

questiontext.text:
Match the compounds involved in the Tricarboxylic Acid (TCA) cycle in List-I with their carbon atom count in List-II.

List-I (Compound)List-II (Carbon Count)
(A) Citric acid(i) 2-carbon acetyl group
(B) \(\alpha\)-ketoglutaric acid(ii) 3-carbon compound
(C) Oxaloacetic acid(iii) 5-carbon compound
(D) Acetyl CoA(iv) 6-carbon compound
(v) 4-carbon compound

Choose the correct match.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
During the TCA cycle, a 2-carbon acetyl group condenses with a 4-carbon acceptor to form a 6-carbon tricarboxylic acid, which is then stepwise decarboxylated back to the 4-carbon acceptor.

Step 2: Evaluation of Carbon Counts
1. Acetyl CoA carries a 2-carbon acetyl group derived from 3-carbon pyruvate.
2. Oxaloacetic acid (OAA) is a 4-carbon compound that initiates the cycle by condensing with the 2-carbon acetyl group.
3. Citric acid is the first stable 6-carbon product formed by this condensation.
4. After the first decarboxylation (\(\text{CO}_2\) removal), 5-carbon \(\alpha\)-ketoglutaric acid is formed.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct pairings are: (A)–(iv), (B)–(iii), (C)–(v), (D)–(i).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_RESPIRATIONINPLANTS_MATCH_Q07 - Stoichiometric yields per glucose in aerobic respiration

questiontext.text:
Match the molecular yields per glucose molecule oxidised in aerobic respiration (List-I) with their exact numerical values (List-II).

List-I (Yield per Glucose)List-II (Number of Molecules)
(A) Gross ATP directly synthesised in glycolysis(i) 38
(B) \(\text{FADH}_2\) synthesised in Krebs' cycle(ii) 8
(C) \(\text{NADH} + \text{H}^+\) synthesised in mitochondrial matrix (link reaction + Krebs' cycle)(iii) 4
(D) Theoretical net gain of ATP in aerobic respiration(iv) 2

Choose the correct match.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
One molecule of glucose yields two molecules of pyruvic acid in glycolysis, which then enter the mitochondrial matrix for complete aerobic oxidation.

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Standard theoretical respiratory balance sheet assumptions apply.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Per glucose molecule: glycolysis produces 2 pyruvic acid molecules; each pyruvic acid generates \(4\,\text{NADH} + 4\,\text{H}^+\) and \(1\,\text{FADH}_2\) in the mitochondrial matrix.

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
1. In glycolysis, 2 ATP are produced from BPGA \(\rightarrow\) PGA and 2 ATP from PEP \(\rightarrow\) pyruvic acid, giving a gross direct synthesis of 4 ATP.
2. In the Krebs' cycle (2 turns per glucose), 1 \(\text{FADH}_2\) is formed per turn, giving 2 \(\text{FADH}_2\).
3. In the mitochondrial matrix (2 pyruvic acids per glucose), 2 \(\text{NADH} + \text{H}^+\) come from the pyruvate dehydrogenase link reaction and 6 \(\text{NADH} + \text{H}^+\) come from the Krebs' cycle, totalling 8 \(\text{NADH} + \text{H}^+\).
4. Under theoretical assumptions, complete aerobic respiration of one glucose molecule yields a net gain of 38 ATP.

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
All four numerical values are distinct and consistent with the NCERT balance sheet. The correct pairings are: (A)–(iii), (B)–(iv), (C)–(ii), (D)–(i).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_RESPIRATIONINPLANTS_MATCH_Q08 - Entry points of substrates in the amphibolic pathway

questiontext.text:
Match the organic molecules in List-I with the form or stage at which they enter the respiratory pathway in List-II.

List-I (Organic Molecule)List-II (Entry Form / Stage)
(A) Fatty acids(i) Enter as pyruvate, acetyl CoA, or Krebs' cycle intermediates after deamination
(B) Glycerol(ii) Converted to glucose and fructose by invertase
(C) Amino acids(iii) Degraded to acetyl CoA before entering
(D) Sucrose(iv) Converted to PGAL (3-phosphoglyceraldehyde)

Choose the correct match.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
While glucose is the favoured respiratory substrate, fats, proteins, and disaccharides can also be respired by entering the amphibolic pathway at specific intermediary stages.

Step 2: Evaluation of Entry Points
1. Fatty acids are first degraded to acetyl CoA and then enter the respiratory pathway.
2. Glycerol enters the glycolytic pathway after being converted to PGAL (3-phosphoglyceraldehyde).
3. Proteins are degraded by proteases into amino acids, which after deamination enter at pyruvate, acetyl CoA, or some stage within the Krebs' cycle depending on their structure.
4. Sucrose is hydrolysed into glucose and fructose by invertase before entering glycolysis.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct pairings are: (A)–(iii), (B)–(iv), (C)–(i), (D)–(ii).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_RESPIRATIONINPLANTS_MATCH_Q09 - Energetics of fermentation and oxidative phosphorylation

questiontext.text:
Match the bioenergetic parameters in List-I with their corresponding values in List-II.

List-I (Parameter)List-II (Value)
(A) Fraction of glucose energy released in fermentation(i) \(2\,\text{H}^+\)
(B) Protons passing through \(F_0\) per ATP synthesised(ii) 3 ATP
(C) ATP produced per NADH oxidised in ETS(iii) Less than 7%
(D) ATP produced per \(\text{FADH}_2\) oxidised in ETS(iv) 2 ATP

Choose the correct match.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Fermentation releases only a small fraction of the energy stored in glucose, whereas oxidative phosphorylation couples proton flow through ATP synthase to high ATP yields from \(\text{NADH}\) and \(\text{FADH}_2\).

Step 2: Evaluation of Bioenergetic Parameters
1. In both lactic acid and alcoholic fermentation, less than 7% of the energy in glucose is released.
2. During chemiosmotic ATP synthesis at Complex V, for each ATP produced, \(2\,\text{H}^+\) pass through the \(F_0\) channel from the intermembrane space to the matrix.
3. Oxidation of one molecule of \(\text{NADH}\) through the ETS yields 3 molecules of ATP.
4. Oxidation of one molecule of \(\text{FADH}_2\) through the ETS yields 2 molecules of ATP.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct pairings are: (A)–(iii), (B)–(i), (C)–(ii), (D)–(iv).
